source_documents.title: Germanium vs Silicon Bridge in Photoinduced Electron Transfer Leading to Blue Emission

reference_evidence_units.quote: Its previously reported silicon analogue (2) displays efficient blue-light emission resulting from photoinduced intramolecular electron transfer (ET) from carbazole to the divinylbenzene moiety through the dimethylsilyl bridge.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 2 (Si)
reference_evidence_units.statement: Blue emission arises from photoinduced intramolecular ET through the Si bridge.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Established in earlier work; remeasured here.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the bridge linking the donor and acceptor parts plays a crucial role in the light-induced electron transfer process, leading to this blue emission from the intramolecular charge-transfer state (ICT)
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 1 and 2
reference_evidence_units.statement: Both compounds emit from the CT state formed by ET.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Efficient photoinduced intramolecular ET through the Si bridge gives the blue CT emission.

mechanism_decisions.rationale: The emitting CT state is formed by the electron transfer itself through a non-conjugated (Si/Ge) bridge; by guideline §3.3 it is not labelled ICT separately.
